title: U.S. House · Texas's 10th District
area: A redrawn district running from the Austin area northeast toward Bryan-College Station in central Texas.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Michael McCaul (R) retired from public office rather than seek re-election following Texas's August 2025 congressional redistricting. Caitlin Rourk won a three-candidate Democratic primary; Chris Gober won a multi-candidate Republican primary.

priorities.text: Affordable, accessible healthcare: lower drug costs, protect coverage for pre-existing conditions, expand mental health care and strengthen the ACA.
Economic opportunity: raise and index the federal minimum wage to the cost of living, expand affordable child care, and protect and strengthen Social Security.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she would permanently extend enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, pursue a public option and protect coverage for pre-existing conditions.
positions.quote: Permanently extend enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies and pursue a public option to give families more affordable coverage choices.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she would raise and index the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: Raise and index the federal minimum wage, so it better reflects the cost of living and economic realities facing working families.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she would expand affordable child care by fully funding federal programs such as the Child Care and Development Block Grant.
positions.quote: Expand affordable child care by strengthening and fully funding federal programs like the Child Care and Development Block Grant.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she would close loopholes so the wealthiest Americans and large corporations pay their fair share.
positions.quote: Make the tax code work for working families by closing loopholes and ensuring the wealthiest Americans and large corporations pay their fair share.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page lists restoring nationwide protections for reproductive freedom by codifying Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Restore nationwide protections for reproductive freedom by codifying Roe v. Wade and protecting access to contraception, IVF, and emergency reproductive care.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she would strengthen Congressional oversight of military action and reaffirm Congress's constitutional role in decisions of war and peace.
positions.quote: Strengthen Congressional oversight of military action and reaffirm Congress's constitutional role in decisions of war and peace.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page says she would oppose federal efforts to expand or subsidize private school voucher programs.
positions.quote: Protect public dollars for public schools and oppose federal efforts to expand or subsidize private school voucher programs, including proposals supported by Texas leaders.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page calls for halting U.S. funding and sales of offensive weapons to Israel while maintaining defensive support.
positions.quote: Halt U.S. funding and sales of offensive weapons to Israel while maintaining defensive support, with much stronger transparency and oversight.

candidates.name: Chris Gober

priorities.text: Secure the border and reduce illegal immigration, crime and drug trafficking, working with the Trump administration.
Oppose what he describes as the 'weaponization' of federal agencies against conservatives.

Says he will cut regulations, expand small-business opportunities, and strengthen rural healthcare access for rural Texans; also calls for AI-infrastructure policy that protects rural electricity rates and local water supplies from large data-center projects.

statements.quote: Crush the cartels by helping President Trump secure our border and empowering Texas law enforcement to halt the invasion of drugs, violence, and gangs into our community.
statements.context: On his campaign website, Key Issues section

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website lists issue headings in general terms; only one statement fit the issue list. No issue-specific stances on abortion, guns, taxes, tariffs or health coverage found on his site. No Candidate Connection survey checked.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Texas, 2026

researchNotes: Neither candidate has held elected office, so there is no official voting or legislative record to report. Biographical details for both candidates come mainly from their own campaign materials and Ballotpedia profiles; no independent news profile was reviewed.
